needed_evidence: INDEPENDENCE NOTE: E50 (the pooled NNT 265 / NNH 210 meta-analysis) includes ASPREE, ARRIVE and ASCEND. A1/A2 (ASPREE), A7 (ARRIVE, ASCEND) and A3/A19 (the pool) are therefore not independent support for C1/C18. E2, E26 and E59 all report the same ASPREE mortality rates. E39 (the microsimulation) takes as inputs the same pooled estimates as E34/E37.

McNeil et al., NEJM 2018, 'Effect of Aspirin on Cardiovascular Events and Bleeding in the Healthy Elderly' (ASPREE): CV composite HR and CI, major hemorrhage and intracranial hemorrhage counts per 1,000 over 4.7 years. Needed to ground C7's HR of about 0.95 and C10.
Guirguis-Blake et al., JAMA 2022, AHRQ evidence review for USPSTF aspirin: absolute events per 1,000 for MI, stroke, major GI bleeding and intracranial bleeding, stratified by age ≥60 or ≥70.
Zheng & Roddick, JAMA 2019 meta-analysis (likely source of NNT 265 / NNH 210): CIs, follow-up, and age-subgroup (≥65/≥70) results.
Dehmer et al., JAMA 2022, USPSTF microsimulation: per-1,000 net CV events and bleeds at ages 60-69 by 10-year risk, and sensitivity to the no-CRC-effect assumption.
ASPREE-XT long-term follow-up (Lancet Oncology / later reports): cancer incidence and mortality beyond 4.7 years, to test a delayed offset.

ESC 2021 Guidelines on CVD prevention in clinical practice: aspirin recommendation for primary prevention by age, including diabetes at high risk. C21/C22 currently rest only on USPSTF and a secondhand ACC/AHA summary.
Arnett et al., 2019 ACC/AHA Primary Prevention Guideline, original text and rationale for the aspirin recommendation (Class IIb for 40-70, III: Harm for >70).
ARRIVE (Gaziano, Lancet 2018) and ASCEND (NEJM 2018) age-stratified (≥60 or ≥65) net results: serious vascular events vs major bleeds per 1,000.

established: C1: In adults 60+ without prior CVD, initiating low-dose aspirin increases net cardiovascular harm: excess major bleeding (GI and intracranial) per 1,000 treated over about 5 years equals or exceeds the MI and ischemic stroke events prevented, under equal or bleeding-weighted severity weights.
C7: In participants aged 70+ (ASPREE), aspirin did not significantly reduce the CV composite (HR about 0.95, CI including 1) over a median of about 4.7 years.
C12: In older adults, aspirin increased all-cause mortality, driven by cancer deaths, in ASPREE (HR about 1.14 overall), with no benefit on disability-free survival.
C18: Under equal weighting of MI, ischemic stroke, and major bleeding, the net effect per 1,000 treated over about 5 years in adults 60+ is harm or zero, not benefit.

C21: USPSTF 2022 recommends against initiating low-dose aspirin for primary prevention in adults 60+ (Grade D), and ACC/AHA 2019 advises against routine use in those over 70 or at increased bleeding risk, citing a bleeding excess that outweighs benefit.
